# Beginner Cheat Sheet: Git and PowerShell

## Part 1: Git

### 1. `git clone`
Downloads a copy of a remote repository, including its full history, into a new folder on your computer.
```shell
git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git
```

### 2. `git status`
Shows which files are new, changed or staged, so you can see what your next commit will save.
```shell
git status
```

### 3. `git add`
Stages a file, which marks its current changes to go into your next commit.
```shell
git add file.txt
```

### 4. `git commit`
Saves a snapshot of your staged changes to the project history, with a short message that says what you changed.
```shell
git commit -m "Add login page"
```

### 5. `git push`
Uploads your new local commits to the remote repository, such as GitHub, so other people can see them.
```shell
git push origin main
```

## Part 2: PowerShell

### 1. `Get-Help`
Shows the built-in help for any cmdlet: what it does, its parameters, and usage examples.
```powershell
Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Examples
```

### 2. `Get-ChildItem`
Lists the files and folders in the current folder or in a folder you name (alias: `ls`).
```powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path . -Filter *.txt
```

### 3. `Set-Location`
Moves you into a different folder so the commands you run next work there (alias: `cd`).
```powershell
Set-Location .\projects
```

### 4. `Get-Content`
Prints the text of a file on the screen so you can read it without opening an editor (alias: `cat`).
```powershell
Get-Content .\notes.txt
```

### 5. `Copy-Item`
Copies a file or folder to a new location and leaves the original where it is (alias: `cp`).
```powershell
Copy-Item .\notes.txt -Destination .\notes-backup.txt
```

## Notes
- The usual Git order is: `git status`, then `git add`, then `git commit`, then `git push`.
- If your repository's main branch is called `master`, use `git push origin master` instead.
- If `Get-Help` shows only the syntax and no examples, run `Update-Help` once to download the full help files.
- The aliases `ls`, `cat` and `cp` work on Windows. In PowerShell on macOS or Linux, those names run the system's own commands instead, so use the full cmdlet names there.

---
Merge log: the two parts did not contradict each other or repeat anything, so both are kept as written, with small wording cuts in Git items 2 and 3. I added the Notes section to cover pitfalls that neither subtask mentioned. The checks behind these notes (default branch name, help files that are not installed by default, aliases that exist only on Windows) come from known PowerShell and Git behavior. I did not run any commands to test them.

issues: 결과물 맨 끝에 merge log(작업 과정 메모: 'Merge log: ... I did not run any commands to test them.')가 붙어 있다. 초보자용 cheat sheet에 들어갈 내용이 아니므로 빼야 한다. 그리고 goal은 두 part를 요구했는데 세 번째 'Notes' section이 생겼다. 이 내용은 각 part 안으로 옮기는 것이 맞다.

Update-Help note가 Windows 기본 셸에서는 그대로 따라 할 수 없다. 이 machine의 Windows PowerShell 5.1.22621에서 직접 확인했다. help 파일이 없으면 `Get-Help Get-ChildItem -Examples`는 예제 없이 이름, alias, remarks만 보여 준다. 5.1의 Update-Help에는 -Scope parameter도 없다(ContainsKey('Scope') = False). 문서상 5.1의 Update-Help는 관리자 권한 session이 필요한데, note에는 그 말이 없다. 관리자 권한 요구는 직접 실행해 보지 않았다. 그래서 초보자가 처음 해 보는 PowerShell 예제가 사실상 동작하지 않는다. 관리자 실행 안내를 넣거나 `Get-Help <cmdlet> -Online`을 대안으로 적는 편이 낫다.
Copy-Item 설명 'Copies a file or folder'는 오해를 부른다. 5.1에서 직접 확인한 결과, -Recurse 없이 `Copy-Item src dst`를 실행하면 빈 folder만 생기고 하위 항목은 0개였다. folder를 복사할 때는 -Recurse가 필요하다는 점을 적어야 한다.
git commit의 흔한 초보자 함정이 빠져 있다. `git config --global user.name`/`user.email`을 설정하지 않으면 첫 commit이 'Please tell me who you are' 오류로 실패한다(Git의 알려진 동작이며 이번에 실행해 보지는 않았다). setup 한 줄이나 note가 필요하다.
git push 관련 안내가 불완전하다. 첫 push 때 GitHub HTTPS 인증(password 대신 PAT나 credential manager 필요)을 언급하지 않는다. 새 branch를 처음 push할 때 필요한 `-u` 설명도 없다. clone한 repo에서는 `git push`만 써도 된다는 점도 빠져 있다. 정도는 경미하다.
명령어 선택에 대해: remote와 함께 작업하는 초보자에게는 `git pull`이 필수에 가깝다. 그런데 clone/status/add/commit/push 다섯 개에서 빠졌고, note에서도 다루지 않는다. 다섯 개를 무엇으로 고를지는 판단의 영역이라 우선순위는 낮다.
확인된 부분: 구조 요구사항(part 2개, part마다 명령어 5개, 각각 한 줄 설명과 예제)은 충족한다. pwsh 7.6에서 ls/cat/cp/cd alias가 해당 cmdlet을 가리키는 것을 확인했다. macOS/Linux alias 동작과 git 관련 주장은 이번에 검증하지 않았지만, 알려진 동작과 맞는다.

gaps: The two subtasks did not contradict or repeat each other. The only merge step was keeping the single '## Part 1: Git' heading from 1.1.1, because 1.1.2 had none.

`git push origin main` only works when the branch is named main. That is GitHub's default, but older repos and some local `git init` setups use master. A plain `git push` would work right after `git clone`, but I kept the subtask's version because it shows the remote and branch explicitly.

Missing prerequisite: `git push` to GitHub needs authentication (a credential manager or a personal access token; GitHub does not accept account passwords for pushes). This is not mentioned.
`git init` (starting a repository without cloning one) and `git pull` (getting other people's changes) are left out on purpose to stay within five entries.

gaps: Merge: I kept 1.2.1's heading and entries 1-3 and 1.2.2's entries 4-5. The two subtasks did not overlap or contradict each other. I changed only wording: entry 2 used to say 'like ls in other shells', which is misleading because ls is a Windows-only alias in PowerShell 7 and not an alias on Linux or macOS. All five entries now use the same '(alias: x)' style. I tightened entries 1 and 3. No example was changed.

What I checked: I ran PowerShell 7.6.9's parser on all five examples and none had syntax errors. Get-Command confirmed that the -Examples, -Filter and -Destination parameters exist, and Get-Alias confirmed that ls, cd, cat and cp point to the cmdlets named. I did not actually run the examples, because .\projects and .\notes.txt are placeholders.

Known limitation: on a fresh Windows install the full help files are not downloaded yet. Until the user runs Update-Help (some modules need an elevated session for this), 'Get-Help ... -Examples' may show only a short auto-generated summary with no examples. Nothing in the cheat sheet tells beginners this.

Choices I made: entry 5 is Copy-Item, not Remove-Item. Remove-Item (alias rm/del) is not covered, nor is any 'make a new folder' command (New-Item or mkdir). Copying is the safer first command for beginners, but they will probably need these other two soon.
Entries 4 and 5 assume .\notes.txt exists in the current folder. Nothing in the sheet creates it first, for example with 'Set-Content .\notes.txt "hello"'.
